FORE WORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Transport Tractors, Trailers and Industrial Trucks Sectional Committee had "been apprcwed by the Transport Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1976. The revision of this standard has been updated based on latest technology development. Every trailer shall be provided with tail lamp% stop lamps and other electrical fittings as required by the relevant Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and the amendments made from time to time. The values of dimensional details and axle loading given in this standard are recommendatory and not intended to over-ride the limitations otherwise laid down by different administrative authorities. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding.off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 8037:2005

Indian Standard GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR TRANSPORT TRACTOR-TRAILERS (First Revision )
1 SCOPE IS No. Title

This standard specifies dimensional and technical requirements of transport tractor-trailers and this standard takes into consideration the handling of 1S.0 Series-I freight containers. This standard does not cover the requirements of special purpose transport tractor-trailers constructed for the conveyance of indivisible loads .of abnormal weight and dimensions, or agricultural tractorstrailers. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below:

TERMINOLOGY

3.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS 7774 (Part .1), IS 7774 (Part 2) and the following shall apply. 3.2 Tandem Axle -- Tandem axle k-defined as any two or more consecutive axles, whose centre are more than 1.3 m but not more than 2.4 m apart and are individually attached to and/or articulated ffom a common attachment to the vehicle"including a connecting mechanism designed to equalize the load between the axles.

9942:1992

`IS 8037:2005 3.3 Transport Tractor-Trailer -- The transport tractortrailer shall be defined as a combination of transport tractor with trailer coupled together permanently or temporarily, designed primarily for the transportation of goods by road. 4 TYPES Transport tractor-trailer shall be classified as follows: a) Tractor with full/drawbar trailer; and b) Tractor with semi/articulated trailer. 5 MATERIAL The materials used for the manufacture shall conform to relevant Indian Standards, wherever available. 6 DIMENSIONAL 6.1 Overall Length The overall length for the tractor-trailer combination shall not exceed 18 m for tractor-trailer combination.
NOTE -- The overall length is measured between the front of the tractor to the rear most part of the trailer, This includes any part(s) projecting in front or rear (towing hooks, bumpers, etc) forming permanent part of the tractor-trailer combination.

8.2.1 Brakes on each axle shall be capable of producing peak retarding force equal to 0.45 times the rated load on the axle. 8.2.2 Each trailer equipped with air or air hydrau!ic brakes shall be fitted with an air reservoir having capacity to give the minimum of four full brake applicaticrns with pressure drop from cut-out to 0.7 times the cut-in pressure. 8.2.3 Each trailer equipped with air or air hydraulic brakes shall be fitted with an emergency brake relay valve. This valve shall be designed to automatically apply the trailer brakes in case the failure in trailer brake coupling arises. 8.2.4 The brakes shall distribute their action appropriately among the axles. 8.2.5 Wear on the brakes must `be capable of being easily taken up by means of a system of manual O+ automatic adjustment. 8.2.6 The brake requirements of the trailer shall conform to IS 11852 (Part 2) to IS 11852 (Part 6) and IS 11852 (Part 8) as applicable. 8.3 Protective
Arrangement

DETAILS

6.2 The overall height of the laden trailer measured from the road surface on which the trailer rests to the maximum point of projection shall not exceed 3.8 m for normal application and 4.2 m when they are carrying 1S0 Series I freight containers or similar indivisible bulky loads. 6.3 The overall width of the transport tractor-trailers measured between the extreme points shall not exceed 2.'7m. `7 AXLE LOADING Maximum axle load shall be 10.2 tonne in the case of single axle and 19 tonne in the case of tandem axle. 8 CONSTRUCTIONAL
DETAILS

Pressure regulator valve and the relay valve shall be installed in the tractor and trailer chassis respectively in twin line braking system to ensure: a) protection to the tractor from loss of complete air pressure in case of accidental uncoupling of the trailer; release of brakes only atler stipulated air pressure is available in the air brake circuit and reservoirs of the tractor and trailer; and automatic brake application of the trailer brake in case of trailer parting from the tractor accidentally.

b)

c)

"8.1 The body of the trailer shall be sturdy and able to

give maximum floor space and capacity. The side boards and tail boards when specified by the purchaser shall be sturdy and fixed or hinged as required. All trailers shall have lashing/anchoring arrangements for tying down load or the cover thereof. 8.2 Service Brakes Each axle on trailers. of capacity over 1 tonne shall be fitted with service brakes which shall be coupled to the service brakes on the tractor and shall be applied on the operation of the foot brake pedal in the tractor. 2

8.3.1 In the event of tractor beirw disconnected from the trailer, the airflow both from tractor and trailer shall be sealed off automatically or by means of a manual shut-off device easy to couple, fitted between the tractor and trailer. 8.3.2 In the case of semi-trailers suitable antijackknifmg device maybe provided subject to the requirements of the purchaser.
NOTE -- Jack-knifing is a violent divergent instability in which the tractor rotates about the king pin with relatively little angular movement of the trailer.

8.4 A parking brake shall be provided with all types of trailers so that it may be applied effectively after

IS 8037:2005 detaching from the drawing vehicle. The parking brake shall hold a fully laden trailer stationary on a 12 percent up and down gradient. 8.5 Identification of Service and Emergency Couplings Service and emergency couplings shall be painted differently (for example yellow for service and red for emergency couplings). 8.6 The suspension shall be such that it absorbs road shocks, ensures smooth running and minimize vibrations. 8.6.1 The suspension in the case of tandem axle shall be so designed as to share the load equally between the axles in tandem. 8.7 The transport tractor-trailers shall be provided with suitable pneumatic tyres of adequate capacity. 8.8 The tow bar shall be parallel as much as possible to the ground on level surface in coupled conditions. However, for cranked tow bars, this shall not be applicable. 8.9 Depending on the load, the king pin conforming to IS 6763 (Part 1) or IS 6763 (Part 2) may be provided. The fifth wheel shall be robust and suitable for the particular king pin on the trailer. The fifth wheel coupling shall conform to IS 8007. 8.10 The values of the angle of approach, angle of departure and ground clearance shall be as agreed to between the -purchaser and the supplier. 8.11 The minimum clearance between the tractor and the trailer shall be such that there is no fouling at any angle of turn. The fifth wheel coupling dimensions for interchangeability shall conform to IS 8007. 8.11.1 The stopping device may also be provided to ensure that such fouling does not take place. 8.12 Rear Under Run -Protective
Device

suitable means to the frame of the trailer and the drawing vehicle, for purposes of retaining connection between the towing vehicle and the trailer in the event of failure of the drawbar or accidental disconnection of the tractor and trailer. The mechanical strength of the safety chain shall be equal to at least double the strength of the drawbar assembly. All other trailers ( 1 tonne and above) shall have ~mergency brakes which shall operate in the event of failure of drawbar or accidental disconnection of the tractor and trailer. 9.1.2 Every trailer shall be fitted with reflex reflectors as specified in the relevant Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 to give indication by the reflected light from the following vehicle. 9.1.3 Every semi-trailer of full trailer with single axle shall be provided with suitable arrangement for keeping the trailer in a level position when detached from the tractor. The arrangement shall be simple and easily accessible and operatable, and shall be provided as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 9.1.4 Supply of tools shall be as agreed to between the p-urchaser and the supplier. In the event of took being supplied a tool box of appropriate dimensions shall be provided. 9.1.5 All parts of the trailer requiring lubrication shall have suitable easily accessible arrangements. 9.1.6 All fasteners shall conform to relevant Indian Standards. 9.-1.7 A suitable sturdy bumper shall be provided at the rear of the trailer chassis. It shall be so located that it does not obstruct the registration plate or any other writing on any of the fittings when viewed from the rear. 9.1.8 Suitable unobstructed location shall be available at the~ear df the trailers chassis for fixing the lift jack when repairs to the axis or the wheels are to be carried out. 9.2 Electrical
9.2.1 Fitments

The transport tractor-trailers shall be provided with a rear under run protective device in accordance with IS 14812 as amended from time to time. 8.13 Side Under Run Protective
Device

The transport tractor-trailers shall be provided with a side under run protective device in accordance with IS 14682 as amended from time to time. 9 GENERAL 9.1 Mechanical Fittings 9.1.1 Every full trailer up to 1 tonne capacity shall be provided with a safety chain which shall be attached by 3

Every trailer shall be provided with tail lamps, stop lamps and other electrical fittings as required by the relevant Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and the amendments made from time to time. 9.2.2 The electrical cables shall be appropriate and shall conform to IS 2465, IS 13461 or IS 13491 as amended from time to time which may be relevant for the type of application. 9.2.3 Easily couplable flexible electrical connections

1S 8037:2005 shall be provided in the trailer. For coupling between any tractor and semi-trailer/full trailer these electrical fittings shall be so located that they do not suffer any damage during the normal operations. 9.2.4 The electrical system voltage shall be 1"2V or 24 V.
10 WORKMANSHIP 10.1 All sharp edges and sharp comers shall be removed. 11 -PAINTING

All painting shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 12 MARKING
12.1 The semi-trailers and trailers shall+e marked with the following. A plate showing the centre of gravity of the unladen trailer shall be provided. a) Manufactures name/trade-mark; b) Type of gross vehicles weight; c) Load carrying capacity (pay load); d) Unladen weight; and e) Load carrying capacity of each axle. 12.2 No fitment or marking shall Qbstruct the function or obliterate any other marking.

10.2 Castings and forgings shall be clean, sound and tlee from defects. 10.3 Welding shall conform to IS 816 and IS 1024 as amended from time to time. 10.4 All wood or metal surfaces coming in contact or faces which become inaccessible after assembly shall be covered with a coat of suitable preservative and appropriate-primer, before assembly.

12.3 Tractor fitted with trailers shall be marked with T-sign plate of dimensions conforming to Indian Standard specification for T-sign plate as per IS 9942. The plate shall be clearly visible at the front of tractor and rear of the trailer.

Standitrds

BI S is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
Copyright

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards :.Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc : No. TED 22 (444).
